51089375.DESCRIPTION: Displacement of 19-mer HIF-1alpha peptide from VHL (unknown origin) by isothermal titration calorimetry analysis
51089375.references_previous: Van Molle, I.; Thomann, A.; Buckley, D. L.; So, E. C.; Lang, S.; M Crews, C.; Ciulli, A. Dissecting Fragment-Based Lead Discovery at the Von Hippel–Lindau Protein–Hypoxia-Inducible Factor 1α Protein–Protein Interface. Chem. Biol. 2012, 19, 1300–1312.

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods: Isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC) experiments were performed on a MicroCal iTC200 instrument (Malvern Instruments, Worcestershire, U.K.) at 25 °C. The VCB complex (100 μM) was loaded into the sample cell, and the 19-mer HIF-1α peptide (1.5 mM) was loaded into the syringe. The peptide was titrated into the protein solution in 20 injections of 2 μL each, with a 120 s spacing between injections. The stirring speed was set to 300 rpm. The buffer used was 20 mM HEPES, 150 mM NaCl, 1 mM TCEP, pH 7.5. The data were analyzed using Origin 7.0 software (MicroCal) with a one-site binding model. The binding affinity (Kd), enthalpy (ΔH), and stoichiometry (n) were determined from the fitted isotherm. The heat of dilution was determined by titrating the peptide into buffer and subtracted from the raw data.
original_paragraph.Figure 3 caption: Figure 3. Detection of 6 binding to VCB using ligand-based NMR spectroscopy. (a–c) NMR spectra for VCB + 6 using set-ups 1 and 2, in red and black respectively, and the compound alone (blue). (d–f) Spectra for VCB + 6 using set-up 3 (green) and compound alone (blue).
original_paragraph.Supporting Information: The ITC experiments were performed as described previously.17
